section_title: Alzheimer's Disease: SST Loss, Amyloid-β and Neprilysin, Tau, and Network Hyperexcitability
thesis: The cortical somatostatin deficit in Alzheimer's disease is the most reproducible observation in this entire literature - independent groups, four decades, three orthogonal assay families, consistent direction. Everything built on top of it is contested: whether SST neurons are lost or preserved, whether somatostatin controls amyloid through neprilysin or by direct interference with aggregation, whether SST cells are hyperactive or structurally degenerating under amyloid, and whether tau preferentially burdens interneurons at all.
scope_notes: AD: SST depletion, SST-neprilysin-Abeta axis, tau, and hyperexcitability; weigh human vs model data.

findings.claim: SST interneuron proportion is negatively associated with amyloid and tau neuropathology and positively associated with cognitive performance proximal to death.

findings.evidence: FDR-corrected association analysis of rCTPs against neuropathology and cognition in ROSMAP.
findings.effect_size: p_FDR = 3.1e-4 for neuritic plaques; p_FDR = 3.9e-6 for rate of cognitive decline

findings.claim: A brain-penetrant somatostatin fusion protein raises hippocampal neprilysin levels, and the neprilysin increase correlates with the fall in Abeta42.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Importantly, the increase in neprilysin levels in the membrane fraction of the hippocampus significantly correlated with the decrease in Aβ42 levels (Figure 5 H).

findings.claim: Cortical somatostatin concentrations are consistently and substantially reduced in Alzheimer's disease postmortem cortex, and more severely than cholecystokinin in the same extracts.

findings.effect_size: 45-65% decrease in somatostatin concentration (vs 24-38% reduction in CCK in 5 of 11 regions)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Somatostatin concentrations measured in the same tissue extracts were consistently decreased by 45 to 65%.
findings.study_system: Human postmortem cerebral cortex (14 AD, 17 age-matched controls)

findings.claim: Somatostatin immunoreactivity is significantly decreased in frontal or temporal cortex of senile dementia of the Alzheimer type, while some subcortical regions such as the nucleus basalis are unchanged.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In cases of senile dementia of Alzheimer type (SDAT), where abundant neurofibrillary tangles and senile plaques (density greater than 30 per 1.3-mm2 field) were present in the cerebral cortex, somatostatin immunoreactivity was found to be significantly decreased in either the frontal or temporal cortex.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay plus reverse-phase HPLC of somatostatin immunoreactivity across cortical and subcortical punches.
findings.effect_size: Significant decrease in frontal or temporal cortex; no change in nucleus of Meynert
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: While there was no change in somatostatin immunoreactivity in the nucleus of Meynert in the SDAT group, tissue punches taken from the amygdala revealed a selective decrease in somatostatin immunoreactivity in the basal nucleus, in the SDAT cases.
findings.study_system: Human postmortem brain (SDAT cases and controls)

findings.claim: Abeta(25-35) lowers somatostatin and neprilysin expression in rat temporal cortex, and minocycline prevents both reductions.
findings.claim_source_sentence:
Minocycline alone enhanced these targets.

Significance

Our findings indicate that minocycline prevents the deleterious effects of Abeta(25-35) on SRIF and neprilysin expression in the rat temporal cortex and that it has protective effects per se on these parameters.
findings.evidence: Pharmacological rescue experiment measuring SRIF and neprilysin expression after intracerebral Abeta(25-35) in rat temporal cortex.
findings.effect_size: Prevention of Abeta-induced reduction (qualitative)
findings.study_system: Rat temporal cortex (in vivo Abeta25-35 infusion)

findings.evidence: Quantitative plaque-density histology across Sst wild-type, hemizygous and null App NL-F/NL-F cohorts at 12 and 15 months.

findings.claim: In the rTg4510 tauopathy model, fast-spiking inhibitory interneurons are selectively hypoactive, and this dysfunction is not explained by intracellular tau accumulation or by loss of Nav1.1 or Kv3.1b.

findings.claim: Late-onset unexplained epilepsy is accompanied by mild cognitive impairment in a substantial minority of patients within five years of seizure onset, supporting a bidirectional link between network hyperexcitability and cognitive decline.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Discussion In this prospective study of participants with late-onset unexplained epilepsy within 5 years of disease onset, we found a 17% prevalence of mild cognitive impairment, with verbal memory being the most affected cognitive domain.
findings.evidence: Prospective cognitive phenotyping with consensus diagnosis in a late-onset unexplained epilepsy cohort.
findings.effect_size: 17% prevalence of mild cognitive impairment
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Based on the consensus meeting, 17% were deemed to have mild cognitive impairment.
findings.study_system: Human patients with late-onset unexplained epilepsy

findings.claim_source_sentence: In sections of Alzheimer's tissue, cortical somatostatin-immunoreactive perikarya exhibited morphological changes consistent with neuronal degeneration.

findings.evidence: Dual-immunolabeling of human Alzheimer's cortex plaques.
findings.study_system: Human postmortem Alzheimer's disease cortex

findings.claim: Somatostatin acts at the sst4 receptor in neocortex to increase amyloid-beta catabolism, and QM/MM refinement of cryo-EM sst4 complexes identifies the residue contacts that determine agonist affinity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Somatotropin-release Inhibiting Factor (SRIF) binds somatostatin subtype-4 receptor (sst4) within the neocortex to increase amyloid beta catabolism, and possibly effects neuronal plaque formation and disease progression of Alzheimer's disease.

findings.claim: Amyloid-beta oligomer injection impairs hippocampal theta and gamma oscillations through dissociable presynaptic deficits, and optogenetic activation of SST interneurons selectively restores theta power while PV activation restores gamma power.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Optogenetic activation of ChR2-expressing SST and PV interneurons selectively restored the peak power of theta and gamma oscillations, respectively, to the levels observed in the control mice, and resynchronized CA1 PC spike phases.

findings.study_system: Mouse (SST-Cre, PV-Cre) hippocampal CA1 in vivo, amyloid-beta oligomer injection

findings.evidence: Whole-cell recordings and optogenetic circuit mapping in acute hippocampal slices treated with AbetaO 1-42.
findings.effect_size: Synapse-specific: PC-to-PV EPSC amplitude significantly decreased while PC-to-SST unchanged
findings.study_system: Mouse hippocampal CA1 slices, AbetaO 1-42 application

findings.claim: Genetic deletion of neprilysin (Mme) in App knock-in mice raises both soluble and insoluble Abeta40/42, and combined neprilysin/IDE deficiency has synergistic effects, consistent with neprilysin accounting for a large fraction of brain Abeta catabolism.

findings.study_system: Mouse brain (cell- and region-specific enzyme expression)

findings.claim: Somatostatin positively regulates neprilysin activity in neurons, and genetic somatostatin deficiency alters hippocampal neprilysin activity and localization while increasing Abeta42, establishing the SST-neprilysin axis as a mechanism linking age-related SST decline to amyloid accumulation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A genetic deficiency of somatostatin altered hippocampal neprilysin activity and localization, and increased the quantity of a hydrophobic 42-mer form of Abeta, Abeta(42), in a manner similar to presenilin gene mutations that cause familial Alzheimer disease.
findings.evidence: Screen of candidate effectors on neprilysin activity in primary cortical neurons plus characterization of somatostatin-deficient mice.
findings.effect_size: Selective upregulation of neprilysin activity by somatostatin among tested effectors; Sst deficiency increased hippocampal Abeta42
findings.study_system: Mouse primary cortical neurons and Sst-knockout mouse hippocampus

findings.claim: In App NL-F/NL-F knock-in mice, somatostatin ablation increases cortical Abeta plaque density without altering whole-brain neprilysin transcript, protein or activity, indicating that somatostatin limits amyloid deposition by interfering with Abeta aggregation rather than through neprilysin induction.

findings.study_system: Mouse (App NL-F/NL-F x Sst knockout) cortex and hippocampus

findings.claim: MicroRNA-181d-5p post-transcriptionally represses neprilysin and simultaneously raises tau, providing a regulatory route by which reduced neprilysin links impaired Abeta clearance to tau pathology.

findings.claim: Somatostatin acts directly on microglia via SSTR2 to enhance phagocytosis and suppress pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and SST overexpression in an AD mouse model lowers microglial density and plaque burden while improving hippocampus-dependent memory.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Furthermore, SST overexpression in an AD mouse model reduced microglial density and amyloid-β plaque burden and improved hippocampus-dependent cognitive performance, indicating a protective effect mediated through microglial modulation.
findings.evidence: Cultured microglia treated with SST plus viral SST overexpression in an amyloid mouse model with histology and behavioural testing.
findings.effect_size: Reduced microglial density and amyloid-beta plaque burden with improved hippocampus-dependent cognitive performance (qualitative in abstract)
findings.study_system: Cultured microglia and AD transgenic mouse model

findings.claim: A few hours of sleep disruption remodels the dendritic spine architecture of SST interneurons in a subregion-specific manner across hippocampus and neocortex, linking a major AD risk factor to the synaptic connectivity of the SST population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Results Dendritic spine density among SST+ interneurons in both hippocampus and neocortex was altered in a subregion-specific manner, with increased overall and thin spine density in CA1, dramatic increases in spine volume and surface area in CA3, and small but significant changes (primarily decreases) in spine size in CA1, PFC, and V1.
findings.evidence: Spine density quantification in SST+ interneurons across hippocampal and neocortical subregions after brief experimental sleep disruption in mice.
findings.effect_size: Increased overall and thin spine density in CA1 with subregion-specific changes elsewhere (qualitative in abstract)
findings.study_system: Mouse hippocampus and neocortex, SST+ interneurons after acute sleep disruption

findings.claim: Treating hAPP transgenic mice with the antiepileptic levetiracetam suppresses aberrant network activity and reverses hippocampal remodeling, synaptic and cognitive deficits, implicating network hyperexcitability as a causal contributor rather than an epiphenomenon.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To explore whether hAPP/amyloid-β-induced aberrant network activity contributes to synaptic and cognitive deficits, we treated hAPP mice with different antiepileptic drugs.

arg_01.thesis: The deficit itself: what is reproducible and what is only directional - Open with the strongest claim in the review and audit it. Reproduced across peptide radioimmunoassay, cell counting and transcriptomic deconvolution, but the magnitudes are measured on non-interconvertible scales and the early cohorts differ in regional panel from near-global (7 of 8 regions) to focal (3 of 21). State the convergence as directional, not quantitative.

arg_02.thesis: Vulnerable or resilient? The same data type, opposite conclusions - Put the deconvolution result (SST the most reduced cell type) against the resilience single-nucleus result (SST+ interneurons selectively preserved and protective) and show the comparator group is doing the work: AD versus unselected controls, versus AD versus cognitively resilient donors at matched pathology. Carry regional disagreement (perirhinal decline versus prefrontal sparing) in the same discussion.

arg_03.thesis: The somatostatin-neprilysin-amyloid axis and its direct refutation - Lay out the causal chain as proposed - somatostatin raises neprilysin activity, neprilysin degrades Abeta42, Sst deficiency raises Abeta42 - and then present the knock-in cross that finds no effect of Sst ablation on neprilysin transcript, protein or activity while plaque density still rises, attributing the effect to direct interference with aggregation. This is the single most consequential unresolved conflict in the review because the therapeutic programme in (sec-therapeutics) assumes the neprilysin link.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_05.thesis: Whether somatostatin controls brain Abeta levels through regulation of neprilysin. The earlier study reports that somatostatin upregulates neprilysin activity and that Sst deficiency alters hippocampal neprilysin activity and raises Abeta42; the later knock-in cross finds no effect of Sst ablation on neprilysin transcript, protein or activity despite increased cortical plaque density, attributing the effect to direct interference with Abeta aggregation.

Direct dispute over whether somatostatin controls Abeta through neprilysin; the therapeutic rationale depends on it. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_09.thesis: Whether somatostatin signalling controls brain neprilysin in vivo: receptor double-knockout work reports loss of SST1/SST4 lowers presynaptic neprilysin and raises hippocampal Abeta42, whereas Sst-ligand knockout in the same App knock-in background reports no change in whole-brain neprilysin transcript, protein or activity while plaque density still rises, implying a neprilysin-independent anti-aggregation mechanism.
arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_09.synthesis: Conflict cluster_03_conf_09 (foreground; resolution_status=open). The receptor-knockout and ligand-knockout results on brain neprilysin disagree in the same App knock-in background. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_03.thesis: Whether SST interneurons are the most vulnerable or a selectively preserved population in AD cortex. Deconvolution of bulk and single-nucleus data reports SST interneuron proportions as the cell type most reduced in AD, whereas the resilience-focused single-nucleus study describes SST+ interneurons as selectively preserved and protective. The dimension is cell-type vulnerability versus resilience, with different comparison groups (AD vs control vs cognitively resilient donors).
arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_03.synthesis: Conflict cluster_03_conf_03 (foreground; resolution_status=open). SST interneurons reported as the most depleted cell type and as selectively preserved, from similar human data types. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): design_rigor_and_statistical_unit.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_08.thesis: Whether SST interneurons are functionally hyperactive or structurally compromised in amyloid models. In vivo imaging reports a 2.7-fold increase in SOM interneuron event rates, while ultrastructural work shows SOM-positive dystrophic neurites at 89% of plaques with near-complete sparing of PV terminals. The two readouts (somatic calcium activity versus axonal/terminal degeneration) may be reconcilable but are reported as opposite directions of SST involvement.
arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_08.synthesis: Conflict cluster_03_conf_08 (foreground; resolution_status=partially_resolved). Functional hyperactivity versus ultrastructural degeneration of the same population. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): model_construct_and_species_transfer.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_10.thesis: Direction of SST interneuron activity change under amyloid: in vivo imaging in plaque-bearing APP/PS1 cortex reports SOM interneuron hyperactivity (2.7-fold higher event rate), while acute soluble Abeta42 oligomer exposure reduces nicotine-evoked activity in SST+ interneurons; differences may reflect fibrillar/chronic versus soluble/acute amyloid and spontaneous versus cholinergically driven activity.
arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_10.synthesis: Conflict cluster_03_conf_10 (foreground; resolution_status=open). Opposite signs of SST activity change under chronic plaque versus acute soluble oligomer exposure. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): model_construct_and_species_transfer.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_01.thesis: Which neuronal class preferentially accumulates pathological tau. The extracellular-vesicle inoculation study finds the majority of AT8-positive cells in mouse hippocampus are GAD67-positive interneurons, whereas the human postmortem and PS19 study finds tau accumulation predominantly in excitatory neurons. The dimension of disagreement is cell-class tropism of tau, confounded by seeded mouse inoculation versus spontaneous human/transgenic pathology and by region (hippocampus vs prefrontal cortex).
arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_01.synthesis: Conflict cluster_03_conf_01 (foreground; resolution_status=open). Cell-class tropism of pathological tau - interneuron-predominant in seeded mouse hippocampus, excitatory-predominant in human cortex. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): species_region_and_circuit_context.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_02.thesis: Whether reduced Nav1.1 in interneurons is the mechanism of inhibitory dysfunction in AD models. The amyloid model attributes PV interneuron failure and network hypersynchrony to reduced Nav1.1, while the tauopathy model explicitly excludes Nav1.1 and Kv3.1b changes as the cause of fast-spiking interneuron dysfunction. The conflict is partly attributable to proteinopathy (amyloid vs tau) and model (hAPPJ20 vs rTg4510).
arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_02.synthesis: Conflict cluster_03_conf_02 (integrated; resolution_status=resolved-by-method). Nav1.1 as mechanism of interneuron failure in amyloid models versus its exclusion in tauopathy. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): model_construct_and_species_transfer.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_04.thesis: Whether somatostatin loss in Alzheimer's disease extends beyond neocortex. One postmortem radioimmunoassay series reports no significant subcortical reductions, while another reports a selective decrease in the basal nucleus of the amygdala with no change in the nucleus basalis of Meynert. The disagreement concerns anatomical extent and depends on which subcortical nuclei were sampled.
arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_04.synthesis: Conflict cluster_03_conf_04 (integrated; resolution_status=open). Anatomical extent of the somatostatin deficit beyond neocortex. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_06.thesis: Whether somatostatin interneuron numbers fall in amyloid mouse models. One study reports a greater than 55% decline in SOM-positive neurons in deep perirhinal layers of APP/PS1 mice between 4 and 6 months; the other finds no reduction in SOM+ neuron number in prelimbic prefrontal cortex of 9-month-old AD model mice, where only PV+ neurons decline. The dimension of disagreement is regional selectivity versus a general SST vulnerability.

arg_conflict_cluster_03_conf_07.thesis: The mechanism by which 40 Hz sensory stimulation improves outcomes. The first attributes benefit to frequency-specific entrainment that lowers Abeta levels and plaque load; the second reports memory restoration in pre-plaque App/MAPT knock-in mice via re-established global network dynamics, explicitly proposing a non-amyloid, not necessarily 40 Hz-specific mechanism.

arg_unanchored.thesis: The cortical somatostatin deficit in Alzheimer's disease is the most reproducible observation in this entire literature - independent groups, four decades, three orthogonal assay families, consistent direction. Everything built on top of it is contested: whether SST neurons are lost or preserved, whether somatostatin controls amyloid through neprilysin or by direct interference with aggregation, whether SST cells are hyperactive or structurally degenerating under amyloid, and whether tau preferentially burdens interneurons at all.

subsections.title: The deficit itself: what is reproducible and what is only directional
subsections.job: Open with the strongest claim in the review and audit it. Reproduced across peptide radioimmunoassay, cell counting and transcriptomic deconvolution, but the magnitudes are measured on non-interconvertible scales and the early cohorts differ in regional panel from near-global (7 of 8 regions) to focal (3 of 21). State the convergence as directional, not quantitative.

subsections.title: Vulnerable or resilient? The same data type, opposite conclusions
subsections.job: Put the deconvolution result (SST the most reduced cell type) against the resilience single-nucleus result (SST+ interneurons selectively preserved and protective) and show the comparator group is doing the work: AD versus unselected controls, versus AD versus cognitively resilient donors at matched pathology. Carry regional disagreement (perirhinal decline versus prefrontal sparing) in the same discussion.

subsections.title: The somatostatin-neprilysin-amyloid axis and its direct refutation
subsections.job: Lay out the causal chain as proposed - somatostatin raises neprilysin activity, neprilysin degrades Abeta42, Sst deficiency raises Abeta42 - and then present the knock-in cross that finds no effect of Sst ablation on neprilysin transcript, protein or activity while plaque density still rises, attributing the effect to direct interference with aggregation. This is the single most consequential unresolved conflict in the review because the therapeutic programme in (sec-therapeutics) assumes the neprilysin link.

subsections.title: Tau, SST interneurons, and cell-class tropism
subsections.job: Weigh seeded-inoculation evidence that most tau-bearing cells are GAD67-positive interneurons against human postmortem and PS19 evidence for predominantly excitatory accumulation; keep seeded-versus-spontaneous and region as the named confounds. Include tau-bearing dystrophic SST survivors as a distinct phenotype from cell loss.

subsections.title: Network hyperexcitability: how much is biology and how much is recording time
subsections.job: Show that estimated hyperexcitability burden in AD varies roughly tenfold with recording intensity, and that the human cohort evidence is a set of heterogeneous readouts with small samples. Then connect to interneuron mechanism: Nav1.1 reduction in amyloid models versus its explicit exclusion in a tauopathy model.

subsections.title: Hyperactive or degenerating? SST interneuron state under amyloid
subsections.job: Present the 2.7-fold increase in SOM event rates alongside SOM-positive dystrophic neurites at 89% of plaques with near-complete sparing of PV terminals, and alongside acute soluble-oligomer suppression of nicotine-evoked SST activity. Argue that somatic calcium activity and axonal integrity are different quantities and that chronic/fibrillar versus acute/soluble amyloid are different exposures.

subsections.title: What the AD evidence can and cannot support
subsections.job: Close with the audited position: a reproducible peptide deficit, a credible but unreplicated causal mechanism with a direct refutation on the record, and no human study that manipulates or longitudinally tracks SST interneuron number alongside amyloid load.

opening_constraint: (sec-selective-vulnerability) established that marker reductions of disease magnitude occur with age and after many insults; AD is where that ambiguity carries a mechanistic hypothesis, because somatostatin is proposed to regulate amyloid clearance directly.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Causal link between SST interneuron loss and amyloid accumulation in human brain
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: No human study in the retrieved set manipulates or longitudinally tracks SST interneuron number alongside amyloid load; the causal direction rests entirely on rodent Sst knockout and agonist studies.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The therapeutic rationale for SST-receptor agonists in AD assumes the rodent causal ordering transfers to humans.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Cell-type-resolved neprilysin measurement in human AD cortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Neprilysin enrichment in interneurons is established in mouse cortex, but no retrieved human study quantifies neprilysin protein or activity specifically within SST or PV interneurons in AD versus control.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: If the Abeta-degrading capacity of the cortex is concentrated in the same interneurons that are lost, SST interneuron loss would amplify amyloid accumulation non-linearly.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Whether SST interneurons are vulnerable or resilient in AD
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Direct reconciliation of deconvolution-based vulnerability estimates with resilience-cohort single-nucleus findings using the same donors, annotation and comparator group.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Opposite conclusions are currently drawn from similar data types, which undermines any quantitative statement about SST interneuron loss magnitude.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Primary experimental demonstration that somatostatin regulates neprilysin in human neurons
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration — the claim that neprilysin is 'regulated by the neuropeptide somatostatin' is repeated across papers and reviews in the retrieved set, but within this frame the original human-tissue demonstration was not identified; all retrieved primary evidence is rodent or cell-culture.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: a widely stated mechanistic premise for SST-based AD therapeutics without a traceable human experimental source in the retrieved evidence.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Interneuron-subtype specificity of network hyperexcitability in AD models
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Nearly all mechanistic rescue evidence targets PV interneurons and Nav1.1; no retrieved study tests whether restoring SST interneuron output alone normalises epileptiform activity.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Section-level claims that link SST loss to hyperexcitability currently rest on PV-cell experiments with SST cells inferred rather than manipulated.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Subclinical epileptiform activity rates in AD
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Prevalence estimates come from small heterogeneous cohorts with different recording modalities and no shared detection criteria; retrieved work explicitly reports that current morphological criteria under-detect.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Any quantitative statement about how common subclinical seizures are in AD is method-dependent and should not be pooled.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: SST-neprilysin axis as the mechanism of SST-dependent amyloid control
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: An independent replication of the original neprilysin-upregulation result in a knock-in amyloid model; the one in vivo test in App NL-F/NL-F x Sst-null mice found no change in neprilysin transcript, protein or activity despite increased plaque density
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: the SST-to-neprilysin-to-Abeta chain is repeated widely in reviews while the only in vivo amyloidosis test of it is negative, which changes how SST loss should be interpreted mechanistically

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Direct measurement of SST interneuron number and activity in the same AD tissue
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Studies that pair cell counts with physiological recording in the same animals or the same human tissue; current evidence sets structural loss studies against calcium-imaging activity studies with no shared preparation
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Without a shared preparation, apparent conflicts between SST hypoactivity (loss) and SST hyperactivity (imaging) cannot be resolved and both are used to support opposite circuit models

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Interneuron-subtype resolution in human AD electrophysiology
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Human evidence connecting subclinical epileptiform activity to a specific interneuron subtype; the 42-64% hyperexcitability rates come from scalp or intracranial EEG with no cell-type identification
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The attribution of human network hyperexcitability to SST or PV interneuron dysfunction rests entirely on mouse models, which disagree about which subtype is affected

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Somatostatin control of neprilysin in vivo
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: A single study that measures neprilysin protein and activity, Abeta species and plaque load side by side in Sst-ligand knockout and Sst1/Sst4 receptor knockout mice on the same App knock-in background
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The ligand-knockout and receptor-knockout results point to opposite mechanisms (direct anti-aggregation vs neprilysin regulation), and the field currently cites both as if they agreed

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Direction of SST interneuron activity change in amyloid models
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Within-animal comparison of spontaneous and cholinergically driven SST interneuron activity across the soluble-oligomer and plaque-bearing stages of the same model
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Hyperactivity and suppression are each reported from different preparations, so the therapeutic polarity (silence vs boost SST cells) cannot currently be settled

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Primary experimental source for 'SST interneuron loss causes network hypersynchrony in AD'
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration that selective reduction of SST interneurons alone is sufficient to produce epileptiform activity; a conditional transcription-factor deletion that reduces SST interneuron density and excitatory drive reported no epileptiform activity
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: the causal step from SST cell loss to hypersynchrony is widely asserted but the available selective-loss model does not reproduce it

evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Modern trials of receptor-subtype-selective agonists; the only human replacement study retrieved used a non-selective analogue and reported no cognitive benefit with reduced cerebral glucose metabolism
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Preclinical SST1/SST4 agonist results are being framed as translational without acknowledging the negative human precedent from non-selective stimulation

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Whether somatostatin controls brain Abeta levels through regulation of neprilysin. Whether somatostatin signalling controls brain neprilysin in vivo: receptor double-knockout work reports loss of SST1/SST4 lowers presynaptic neprilysin and raises hippocampal Abeta42, whereas Sst-ligand knockout in the same App knock-in background reports no change in whole-brain neprilysin transcript, protein or activity while plaque density still rises, implying a neprilysin-independent anti-aggregation mechanism.

Whether SST interneurons are the most vulnerable or a selectively preserved population in AD cortex. The dimension is cell-type vulnerability versus resilience, with different comparison groups (AD vs control vs cognitively resilient donors).

Whether SST interneurons are functionally hyperactive or structurally compromised in amyloid models. In vivo imaging reports a 2.7-fold increase in SOM interneuron event rates, while ultrastructural work shows SOM-positive dystrophic neurites at 89% of plaques with near-complete sparing of PV terminals. The two readouts (somatic calcium activity versus axonal/terminal degeneration) may be reconcilable but are reported as opposite directions of SST involvement.

Direction of SST interneuron activity change under amyloid: in vivo imaging in plaque-bearing APP/PS1 cortex reports SOM interneuron hyperactivity (2.7-fold higher event rate), while acute soluble Abeta42 oligomer exposure reduces nicotine-evoked activity in SST+ interneurons; differences may reflect fibrillar/chronic versus soluble/acute amyloid and spontaneous versus cholinergically driven activity.

Which neuronal class preferentially accumulates pathological tau. The extracellular-vesicle inoculation study finds the majority of AT8-positive cells in mouse hippocampus are GAD67-positive interneurons, whereas the human postmortem and PS19 study finds tau accumulation predominantly in excitatory neurons. The dimension of disagreement is cell-class tropism of tau, confounded by seeded mouse inoculation versus spontaneous human/transgenic pathology and by region (hippocampus vs prefrontal cortex).
